record.paper: Sublinear separators in intersection graphs of convex shapes

dossier_meta.paper: Sublinear separators in intersection graphs of convex shapes
dossier_meta.statement_text: Given a polynomial $p$, do there necessarily exist real numbers $c, s \geq 1$ and a positive integer $d$, such that the following holds: every graph $G$ satisfying $\mathrm{col}_r(G) \leq p(r)$ for every non-negative integer $r$ admits a $(c, \sqsubseteq_s)$-tame representation in $\mathbb{R}^d$?
dossier_meta.context_text: Theorem 4 shows that graphs with $(c,\sqsubseteq_s)$-tame representations in $\mathbb{R}^d$ have strong coloring numbers bounded by $\delta r^d$, paralleling Krauthgamer–Lee's characterization (Theorem 5) of polynomial-growth graph classes via grid embeddings. Answering Question 6 would determine whether Theorem 4 yields an analogous geometric characterization of graphs with polynomially bounded strong coloring numbers.
